# Chapter 2 (M1) — A working pipeline and what 4B training costs

*Milestone M1, 28 October – 3 November 2026. Tables are generated by `scripts/report_m1_tables.py`
from the committed reports in `docs/reports/`; decisions are in `docs/decisions/`, the gate memo is
`docs/gates/G0.md`.*

## 2.1 Purpose

M1 has two jobs. Lane B builds the training pipeline end to end and shows, on the development model
Qwen3.5-2B-Base, that it trains, resumes and logs what the project rules require. Lane A measures
what 4B RL training costs on its target hardware (4×A40 on fc098), so that Gate G0 can fix one
training mode for every algorithm and the plan's schedule can be checked against measured rates.
**Nothing in this chapter counts toward the study's conclusions.** The 2B runs are development
runs, and the 4B runs measure memory and speed, not learning.

**Outcome.** The four exit criteria are met. GRPO on 2B-Base raises training reward by 5.9
standard errors over 37 steps, and evaluation behaviour stays sensible. A deliberately killed job
resumes with continuous metrics. G0 fixes full BF16 for every 4B run (SFT, DPO and RL) on 4×A40.
At 9.28M rollout tokens per hour, budgets of 30–50M tokens take 3.2–5.4 h and 100–200M take
10.8–21.5 h, one job each. Lane A then needs 10–26 days for M2–M8, well under the plan's 40–60,
and evaluation on Lane B becomes the limit. M1 used 229.8 GPU-hours, all on A40, A30 and A10.

## 2.2 Pipeline

What now exists and is tested (decisions 012–024):

- **Config.** `ExperimentConfig` reads the frozen protocol from the suite file: prompt, thinking
  mode, FP8 KV cache and the 16,384-token cap. An RL config therefore cannot sample differently
  from evaluation. Validators reject a KL term (decision 013), a raised cap, and LoRA on the
  vision tower or the MTP head.
- **Data.** RL data v3.1 has 11,868 training problems. A 256-problem in-loop validation split is
  carved from RL train v3 (decision 012). For every row and both Qwen models, the prompt token ids
  verl builds equal those of the evaluation sampler.
- **RL.** `main_rl` drives verl 0.9.1 from the config. Rollouts sample at temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0
  for every algorithm (017). A rollout truncated at the cap gets reward 0 (014). Each step makes 4
  optimizer updates on mini-batches of whole groups (022), and a rollout failure stops the run
  (016). The pinned stack needed three patches: vLLM's FP8 KV wake-up on hybrid models (015), a
  vision-tower freeze that verl ignores (019), and a 4,096 MiB weight-sync bucket against an IPC
  crash (024).
- **Checkpoints.** A save every N steps records its cumulative rollout tokens (013). It is exported
  to HF format in the training job, with LoRA merged in FP32, and older FSDP shards are pruned
  (018). Exports are what Lane B evaluates.
- **Stopping.** A run stops at its rollout-token budget, re-estimated at each save (020). M1.11
  found that verl fixes its last step when that step starts, so a run could end one step short.
  `train_to_stop` now relaunches verl in the same job from the last save (020 revision). It has
  run only in CPU tests; its first GPU use is in M2.
- **Metrics.** Every mandatory metric is written per step from per-rollout records (021), and a
  checker fails a run that misses one.
- **Tests.** Unit tests cover what silently breaks RL: the verifier and reward on 200 fixtures,
  loss masking and aggregation, advantages, pass@k and checkpoint resume. All 302 tests pass inside
  the image (job 3231291).
- **SFT.** TRL trains on pre-tokenized prompt/completion examples, and BF16 LoRA is merged into the
  base layout (023). M2 adds the full-BF16 path that G0 requires.

## 2.3 Resume (exit criterion 2)

A 2B GRPO run was cancelled after step 8. Its chained successor job, on the same node and GPUs,
resumed it from the step-6 save. An identical control ran alongside without interruption.

| Check (2B; killed after step 8, resumed from the step-6 save) | Result |
|---|---|
| two job segments, same node and hardware | True |
| steps continuous (test, control) | True |
| dataloader position restored at every step | True |
| learning rate equal to the control at every step | True |
| optimizer steps (test / control) | 12 / 12 |
| rollout tokens increasing; manifest equals a recount | True |
| step 7 `actor/entropy`: test − control vs the control's largest step change | 0.0138 vs 0.1287 (within) |
| step 7 `actor/grad_norm`: test − control vs the control's largest step change | 0.0018 vs 0.0076 (within) |
| step 7 `critic/score/mean`: test − control vs the control's largest step change | 0.0020 vs 0.1621 (within) |

At step 12 the test had counted 73,333,805 rollout tokens and the control 73,437,481. Rollouts are
not bitwise reproducible between jobs, so the comparison is against the control's own
step-to-step variation, not exact equality. The test found one bug. verl prunes only the saves of
its own process, so the resumed job kept all four FSDP shards. Pruning now works from what is on
disk (decision 018 amendment), and M1.9's resumed run confirmed the fix on GPUs.

## 2.4 2B development run (exit criterion 1)

Qwen3.5-2B-Base, BF16 LoRA rank 64, learning rate 1e-5, 64 prompts × 8 per step, on 2×A40, one
seed. The run stopped at its 20 h development cap after 37 steps and 211.9M rollout tokens; it was
killed once at step 10 and resumed. Saves at steps 12, 24 and 37 were evaluated on a frozen
121-problem development subset (96 Level A, 25 Level B; 16 samples each).

Training reward (mean over the first and last 20% of steps):

| Steps | Window (steps) | First-window reward | Last-window reward | Difference | × its SE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 37 | 7 | 0.331 | 0.477 | 0.146 | 5.9 |

| Level | Checkpoint | Problems | pass@1 | pass@4 | pass@16 | maj@16 | truncated | mean tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | base | 96 | 0.408 | 0.561 | 0.656 | 0.542 | 0.511 | 10,074 |
| A | step 12 | 96 | 0.432 | 0.581 | 0.698 | 0.594 | 0.481 | 9,614 |
| A | step 24 | 96 | 0.479 | 0.638 | 0.740 | 0.698 | 0.434 | 9,450 |
| A | step 37 | 96 | 0.527 | 0.677 | 0.750 | 0.708 | 0.374 | 8,820 |
| B | base | 25 | 0.395 | 0.677 | 0.840 | 0.680 | 0.507 | 11,100 |
| B | step 12 | 25 | 0.438 | 0.712 | 0.880 | 0.760 | 0.430 | 9,953 |
| B | step 24 | 25 | 0.515 | 0.766 | 0.880 | 0.760 | 0.370 | 9,730 |
| B | step 37 | 25 | 0.585 | 0.861 | 0.920 | 0.840 | 0.258 | 8,840 |

Change against the base model, paired over problems (mean ± standard error):

| Checkpoint | Level | pass@1 (points) | pass@16 (points) | truncated (points) | mean tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| step 12 | A | +2.4 ± 1.0 | +4.2 ± 2.5 | -3.0 ± 1.0 | -461 |
| step 12 | B | +4.2 ± 2.2 | +4.0 ± 4.0 | -7.8 ± 1.8 | -1,147 |
| step 24 | A | +7.2 ± 1.4 | +8.3 ± 3.2 | -7.7 ± 1.6 | -624 |
| step 24 | B | +12.0 ± 3.5 | +4.0 ± 4.0 | -13.8 ± 3.0 | -1,370 |
| step 37 | A | +12.0 ± 1.8 | +9.4 ± 3.0 | -13.7 ± 1.8 | -1,254 |
| step 37 | B | +19.0 ± 3.8 | +8.0 ± 5.5 | -25.0 ± 4.3 | -2,261 |

Transitions from the base model to step 37 (a problem counts as solved at k when its pass@k
estimate reaches 0.5):

| Level | k | solved→solved | unsolved→solved | solved→lost | unsolved→unsolved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | 39 | 12 | 1 | 44 |
| A | 16 | 63 | 9 | 0 | 24 |
| B | 1 | 10 | 8 | 0 | 7 |
| B | 16 | 21 | 2 | 0 | 2 |

The run passes every acceptance check: reward rises, no level's pass@1 drops, every stopped sample
is boxed, and truncation does not rise. The gains come with shorter answers, though. Truncation
falls by 14 points on Level A and 25 on Level B, so part of the pass@16 gain may be fewer
truncations rather than new capability. With one seed and 25–96 problems per level, this shows
only that the pipeline learns, which was the question.

## 2.5 4B memory study

Each training mode ran on 4×A40 (fc098) from 4B-Base, with 64 prompts × 8 per step. Values are the
mean ± SD over steps 2–5 of one run each. The knobs were found by a descending search over rollout
tensor parallelism × `gpu_memory_utilization` (decision 024): TP 1 at 0.7 fit and was fastest in
both modes.

| Cell | Mode | TP | util | rollout tok/s | step s | update s | GPU peak, gen (MiB) | KV tokens/replica | headroom | KV peak | preemptions | host RAM (GiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B-F0 | full_bf16 | 1 | 0.7 | 6,469 ± 229 | 1,655 ± 84 | 720 ± 34 | 47,652 | 1,050,624 | 0.45 | 76% | 0 | 103 |
| B-L | lora_bf16 | 1 | 0.7 | 5,853 ± 199 | 1,738 ± 84 | 705 ± 39 | 43,810 | 1,079,808 | 0.46 | 74% | 0 | 206 |

- **Full BF16 rolls out 10% faster.** LoRA decodes through vLLM's adapter kernels. Update time is
  equal within noise, so a full-BF16 step is 5% shorter.
- **Memory is tight in generation.** Full BF16 leaves 1.5 GB of the 48 GB free on the GPU, which is
  the main risk for later runs (G0 names the response). The KV cache has 45% headroom and nothing
  was preempted.
- **LoRA used twice the host RAM** (206 against 103 GiB of the node's 250).
- **Not measured:** the 2×A100 fallback (run only on request), and anything about learning.

## 2.6 Throughput and wall-clock (exit criterion 4)

One 7 h run per mode measured the effective rate R: rollout tokens over all the job's wall-clock,
including start-up, saves, exports and validation. Spread is the coefficient of variation of the
per-step rates (steps 2 onwards).

| Run | Mode | Steps | Wall-clock h | Rollout tokens | R (tokens/h) | steps / validation / other (h) | mean length (run, base) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| m1_throughput_bf0_qwen35-4b | full_bf16 | 14 | 7.01 | 65.1M | 9.28M ± 1.8% | 6.32 / 0.42 / 0.28 | 8,998, 10,132 |
| m1_throughput_bl_qwen35-4b | lora_bf16 | 12 | 6.55 | 57.3M | 8.75M ± 0.9% | 5.88 / 0.31 / 0.37 | 9,244, 10,312 |

Wall-clock for the plan's budgets in full BF16. The last column rescales R to answers 0.5–1.5× the
base model's length; a fit of step time on length gives the rescaling, and those lengths lie
outside what the run covered, so read it as a model.

| Budget | hours | range (spread) | jobs | × 1.25 | at 0.5–1.5× length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30M | 3.2 | 3.2–3.3 | 1 | 4.0 | 3.1–3.5 |
| 50M | 5.4 | 5.3–5.5 | 1 | 6.7 | 5.1–5.9 |
| 100M | 10.8 | 10.6–11.0 | 1 | 13.5 | 10.2–11.8 |
| 200M | 21.5 | 21.2–21.9 | 1 | 26.9 | 20.5–23.6 |

GPUs were busy in every phase (95–99% utilization), and the update reached 0.35 MFU, so no profile
was needed. The rollout/trainer gap under FP8 KV (`rollout_corr/kl`) was 0.00063 per step on 4B,
so rollout correction stays off.

## 2.7 Schedule

`scripts/g0_schedule.py` turns the plan's run counts and budgets (inputs and marked assumptions in
`scripts/g0_schedule.yaml`) into Lane A hours and Lane B days per milestone. Lane A uses R's range
above. SFT and DPO use the measured update rate. Every ~3 h save of an RL run gets one full
evaluation on Lane B, priced from M0's v3 base-model evaluation per GPU type (from its shard claim
and completion times):

| GPU | Shards | Shard-hours | Completion tokens | tok/s | relative to A40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A40 | 51 | 37.9 | 248.6M | 1,823 | 1.00 |
| A30 | 27 | 25.2 | 137.8M | 1,517 | 0.83 |
| A10 | 18 | 26.6 | 101.5M | 1,061 | 0.58 |

One full evaluation is 488M completion tokens, or 74.3 A40-hours. Lane B is run on three pools:
every A30 and A10; those plus fc096/fc097's four A40s (the 16-GPU QOS cap while fc098 trains); and
also fc098 when no Lane A run holds it. Ranges run from the plan's low to its high budgets.

| Milestone | Lane A h (× 1.25) | evaluations | Lane B days, a30_a10 | Lane B days, with_fc096_fc097 | Lane B days, with_fc098 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M2 SFT | 6.5–26.0 | 1 | 0.5 | 0.3 | 0.2 |
| M3 screening | 15.4–29.4 | 8 | 4.1–5.8 | 2.9–4.1 | 2.1–2.9 |
| M4 DPO | 12.5–41.6 | 1 | 0.5 | 0.3 | 0.2 |
| M5 seed 1 | 38.4–88.3 | 12–24 | 5.4–10.9 | 3.8–7.7 | 2.7–5.4 |
| M6 seeds 2-3 | 76.8–176.7 | 24–48 | 10.9–21.8 | 7.7–15.4 | 5.4–10.9 |
| M7 ablations | 38.4–117.8 | 12–32 | 5.4–14.5 | 3.8–10.3 | 2.7–7.3 |
| M7 group size | 11.5–22.1 | 6 | 2.7 | 1.9 | 1.4 |
| M8 Gemma | 32.1–127.3 | 10–26 | 4.5–11.8 | 3.2–8.3 | 2.3–5.9 |

| Lane B pool | GPUs | A40-equivalents | Lane B days (every save / ≤ 4 per run) | critical path days (every save / ≤ 4 per run) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a30_a10 | 4 A30, 6 A10 | 6.82 | 34.1–68.4 / 34.1–37.5 | 34.2–70.3 / 34.2–40.2 |
| with_fc096_fc097 | 4 A40, 4 A30, 4 A10 | 9.66 | 24.1–48.3 / 24.1–26.5 | 24.3–50.5 / 24.3–30.8 |

| Lane A (fc098), M2–M8 | 4 A40 |  | 9.7–26.2 (× 1.25) |  |

Lane A is no longer the constraint: 10–26 days against the plan's 40–60. Lane B is. Evaluating
every save takes 24–48 days with the A40 pairs and 34–68 without them. Capping evaluations at four
per run brings this to 24–27 and 34–38 days. With M0–M1's two weeks, SFT data work, gates and
write-up, the study plausibly ends in 8–13 weeks with the A40 pairs on Lane B, and 9–16 without.
G1 fixes the evaluation cadence. **Weak inputs:** SFT and DPO times come from the RL update rate,
Gemma 4 E4B is not measured (up to 1.5× the 4B time is assumed), and each pool is a scenario, not
a reservation.

A first draft of the memo priced an evaluation at M0's 90.3 GPU-hours spread over 10 equal
workers, giving 28–57 days. That mixed GPU types: those GPU-hours were partly A40 time, while the
assumed workers were slower A30s and A10s. It was corrected to A40-hours before sign-off.

## 2.8 Gate G0

Every 4B algorithm (GRPO, Dr.GRPO, DAPO, RS-GRPO, DPO), and the SFT they start from, trains in full
BF16 on 4×A40 (fc098). When fc098 is unavailable, runs wait. A whole comparison block moves to
2×A100 only on request. Development runs use Qwen3.5-2B-Base. Full BF16 was chosen for speed and
host RAM, and so that a sharpening result cannot be blamed on a low-rank adapter. Decision 025
fixes the shared 4B base config, the frozen image and the library versions; algorithm configs may
differ only in their decision-001 switches and the M7 group size. Signed off 2026-11-03.

## 2.10 Limitations and what moves on

- **Nothing shows whether full BF16 learns better than LoRA at 4B.** The M1.11 validation rises
  are one seed per mode at different learning rates, so they are no comparison.
- **One run per cell.** The spreads are over steps, not over seeds, nodes or days.
- **The stop-rule fix has not run on GPUs.** Its first use is M2's first RL-style run.
- **Estimated, not measured:** SFT and DPO times (from the RL update rate), Gemma 4 E4B, and the
  2×A100 fallback (full BF16 there would very likely need optimizer offload).
- **Lane B capacity is a scenario.** The A40 pairs are shared with 2B development work.
- **Before M3:** fix learning rate, warmup and weight decay (a decision-025 revision); add a CPU
  test that algorithm configs differ only in their decision-001 switches; give Dr.GRPO a constant
  `loss_scale_factor`.
- **In M2:** the full-BF16 SFT path with resume and periodic checkpoints, the SFT-pool
  contamination report, and the first GPU use of `train_to_stop`. G1 sets the evaluation cadence.
